closing_added.speaker: user
closing_added.message: Thank you. Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses. We may follow up. Anything to add or correct?

closing_added.speaker: expert
closing_added.message: No, I don't have anything to add.

skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At the outset (T2) the interviewer stated the Committee and company are the clients, that they do not represent the witness personally, are not his attorney, and cannot give him legal advice.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explained that the privilege belongs to the company, the company decides whether to waive it, and it may disclose what is learned without the witness's consent.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 set out how the interview would proceed, asked for complete answers, told the witness to flag speculation, and asked him to separate recollection from reconstruction.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asked whether he understood and had questions, and T4 asked him to restate who was represented and who controls privilege before continuing; T5 confirmed.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T356 gave confidentiality, record-keeping and no-contact reminders and asked 'Anything to add or correct?', but did not cover next steps in detail.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
The company decides whether to waive it, and it may disclose what we learn, including to the government, without your consent and without telling you.
Asked the witness to restate in his own words who the firm represents and who controls the privilege; he confirmed the company does.
Explained the interview structure, asked for complete answers, told him to flag speculation and say whether he was reconstructing, and asked if that was acceptable.
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses. We may follow up. Anything to add or correct?

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations such as T16 and T32 let the witness walk through events, though several later topics were pushed with narrow questions.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The interview moved from role (T8) to general process to specific transactions and then to documents, in a sensible order.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are clear and single-focus, such as T56 and T86, though a few, such as T218, bundle two points.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The tone stayed neutral and courteous while the witness was challenged, for example at T252 and T306.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer changed approach when answers called for it, such as T82 asking how the witness knew and T84 asking for a specific deal, and T114 narrowing a vague answer.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Tell me everything you remember about how the hedge was unwound.
Started with the witness's role and moved from general process questions to specific transactions.
How do you know they reviewed every transaction?
Take Raptor I. What did Mr. Causey and Mr. Buy actually review before they signed its approval sheet?
That spring you negotiated the Rhythms unwind and the Southampton purchase for LJM. How does that fit with the three-hours estimate?

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Inconsistencies were pursued well (T148, T252, T306), but the witness's deflection on Andersen's role at T263 and the 'perfectly capable' answer at T107 were not pressed.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The who, what, when and how of the Foundation investment, the Chewco buyout and the Raptor approvals were largely covered.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: T62 asked whether notes or minutes could help, and documents were used at T70 and T300 to refresh memory.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer repeatedly asked how the witness knew things (T56, T82, T346) and the witness's secondhand knowledge was separated (T57, T235).

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: T336 and T342 asked who else to speak with, and T41-T43 pursued the Causey group's reviewers.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: The interviewer identified the minutes, deal files, approval sheets and the witness's personal notes and emails (T62, T349, T352-T354).

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: T116-T119 and T144-T147 tested how certain the witness was about figures and asked where the exact amounts were recorded.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Material answers were followed up (T114, T142), but some were not pursued, such as Jordan Mintz at T323 and the Raptor I sheet at T103.

moments.text: How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
Is there anything that would help you remember, such as notes, minutes, or a presentation from that call?
Approximately, then. Were they above or below the 30 percent the Board was shown?
How certain are you of that figure?
Earlier you said you told the Board you would not receive any current or future value from the Enron stock in LJM. Is that still your recollection?
The minutes record you saying there had been "tremendous utilization" of Raptor I. Our information is that Talon hadn't yet done any derivatives with Enron. Help me understand how those fit together.
The witness deflected a question on LJM2's at-risk status to Andersen, and the interviewer moved on without pressing the point.
Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?
How do you know that: did you see it yourself, or did someone tell you?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: Documents were selected for their relevance, and the interviewer established authorship and provenance before using them (T72, T132, T196, T300).

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: The interviewer generally elicited the witness's account before showing documents (for example T62-T69 before T70), though the Raptor sheets were shown after limited narrative.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: Document descriptions were accurate, for example the 'tremendous utilization' quote at T252 and the 193%/278%/2,500% figures at T200 matched the source.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked the witness to reconcile the documents with his account (T306, T150) rather than drawing conclusions, though some questions framed the conflict fairly directly.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: The witness was given room to explain differences (T253, T307), and the interviewer summarised his position and asked if it was fair (T332-T333).

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
Who prepared them?
I'm now going to show you a document: a partnership agreement for Southampton Place, dated March 20, 2000. Do you recognize it?
I'm not suggesting you wrote it. Do you recognize it?
Earlier you told me you stayed out of the Chewco buyout. This note, addressed to "Andy," refers to $10.5 million for the buyout. Help me understand how those fit together.
So your account is that you don't recall authorizing the payment, and you may have asked that it be resolved after counsel advised there was no basis for it. Is that fair?

missed_opportunities: T321: The witness named Jordan Mintz as the in-house lawyer on the summer 2001 call about the $2.6M payment, but the interviewer did not ask whether counsel's advice was documented or whether Mintz should be interviewed.

T229: The witness said McMahon raised concerns about negotiating against LJM while reporting to him, and the interviewer did not ask what McMahon's specific concerns were or whether the witness had considered stepping aside from those negotiations.
tips: When a witness says counsel gave advice, ask: What exactly did the lawyer say, who else was on the call, and is there any written record of that advice?
Before showing a document, ask: What do you remember about this subject without looking at anything, and what would you expect the document to say?
